steps.say: Lupus is the attacker of every cardiac layer through immune complexes. Pericardium, myocardium, valves, and coronaries are involved together. This figure is the display of the four-layer injury. Active serology with any cardiac symptom is treated as a flare.
steps.tx: Systemic lupus hits all four cardiac layers: **pericarditis** as the commonest lesion, myocarditis with troponin leak and conduction blocks, **Libman-Sacks** sterile vegetations on mitral and aortic valves, and premature coronary atherosclerosis multiplying infarction risk in young women. Each layer below carries its own signature and therapy, from NSAIDs with colchicine for the sac to anticoagulation for vegetations. This figure is the map of the four-layer territory. New chest pain, breathlessness, murmur, or ECG change in lupus is active cardiac disease until proven otherwise.

vis.alt: Diagram of heart showing lupus effects: pericarditis, myocarditis, Libman-Sacks endocarditis on valves, and accelerated atherosclerosis in coronary arteries.
vis.caption: Lupus affects all cardiac layers: pericardium, myocardium, endocardium, and vessels. Each layer below has its own signature. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Sterile valve masses with stroke in lupus are Libman-Sacks vegetations until proven otherwise. Both atrial and ventricular surfaces are coated on left-sided valves. High-titer antiphospholipid antibodies are found in most cases. Embolic events are treated with long-term warfarin.
steps.tx: **Libman-Sacks** endocarditis lays sterile verrucous vegetations of fibrin and platelets on **mitral** valves more than aortic, coating both atrial and ventricular faces of the leaflets. Heavy linkage with high-titer **antiphospholipid** antibodies separates it from culture-negative infective endocarditis, and the masses throw strokes while risking superinfection. Transoesophageal echo finds what transthoracic misses. After embolism, lifelong **warfarin** anticoagulation with valve surgery for large mobile masses is the rule.

steps.say: Coronary disease in rheumatoid arthritis is accelerated by inflammation itself. The infarction risk is raised to one and a half to two times the normal level. CRP with TNF-alpha is measured as the driver of endothelial injury. Lipid with blood pressure targets are set from diagnosis.
steps.tx: Chronic synovitis ages arteries early: rheumatoid arthritis multiplies **myocardial infarction** risk **1.5 to 2.0-fold**, driven by **CRP** and **TNF-alpha** inflammation injuring endothelium and destabilizing plaque apart from Framingham factors. Tight DMARD control lowers the surplus risk, while smoking, hypertension, and dyslipidaemia keep their own targets. Cardiology review with lipid and pressure thresholds applies from the first rheumatology visit, because joints with coronaries share one inflammatory fire.

steps.say: Heart failure with thick walls and tiny ECG complexes is amyloid until proven otherwise. Low voltage against walls above 12 mm is measured as the classic mismatch. Apical sparing on strain imaging is found in both AL and ATTR forms. Bone scintigraphy is performed to confirm transthyretin disease.
steps.tx: **Cardiac amyloidosis**, AL and ATTR types, stiffens the heart into **restrictive cardiomyopathy** with concentric biventricular thickening and rapidly progressive failure. Low limb-lead voltage discordant with wall thickness above **12 mm** is the signature, with **apical sparing** on longitudinal strain where basal segments fail first. Pyrophosphate scintigraphy confirms ATTR without biopsy in the right setting, while AL disease needs urgent haematology referral for plasma-cell therapy.

steps.say: A slow fetal heart with a lupus mother is congenital heart block until proven otherwise. Maternal anti-Ro antibodies are carried across the placenta into the fetal heart. The AV node is replaced by fibrosis after autoimmune myocarditis. Pacing with hydroxychloroquine for later pregnancies is required.
steps.tx: A fetal bradycardia that never varies is **complete congenital heart block**, third-degree AV block from maternal **anti-Ro/SSA**, chiefly **52-kDa Ro**, with anti-La/SSB companions crossing the placenta and binding fetal **L-type calcium channels**. Autoimmune myocarditis scars into AV nodal fibrosis, so most infants need permanent pacing from birth. Later pregnancies carry about 20 percent recurrence, lowered by maternal **hydroxychloroquine** through every subsequent pregnancy.

steps.say: Pulseless arms with heart failure in a young woman are Takayasu arteritis until proven otherwise. The coronary ostia with the ascending aorta are narrowed and dilated together. PET-CT with MR angiography is performed to map activity and stenosis. Bypass grafting is delayed until inflammation is controlled.
steps.tx: **Takayasu arteritis** inflames the aorta with its branches, causing **ostial coronary** stenosis that starves the heart and **ascending aortic** dilation that leaks the aortic valve into failure in young females. Arm claudication with pulseless brachials and bruits points arch-ward. **18F-FDG PET-CT** shows mural uptake while **MR angiography** maps stenosis with wall edema, and this figure is the display of the arch lesions. Immunosuppression quiets the wall before any bypass, because grafts sewn into fire occlude.

vis.alt: Anatomical diagram of the aorta and its major branches, highlighting common sites of Takayasu arteritis pathology such as stenosis, occlusion, aneurysm, and wall thickening in the aortic arch, subclavian, carotid, and renal arteries.
vis.caption: Takayasu arteritis: arch stenosis with aneurysm and wall thickening. Ostial coronary disease with aortic dilation threatens young hearts. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Eosinophilic hearts that fibrose and clot are EGPA until proven otherwise. Myocarditis with apical thrombus is found in ANCA-negative granulomatosis with high eosinophil counts. Scleroderma hearts are scarred by microvascular spasm called cardiac Raynaud. Fibrosis with ventricular arrhythmia is detected by late gadolinium enhancement. Systemic sclerosis is diagnosed when skin thickening with Raynaud and antibodies combine.
steps.tx: **EGPA** cardiac disease kills more patients than any other organ hit, above **50 percent** of deaths, through **eosinophilic myocarditis** with troponin leak, **endomyocardial fibrosis**, and **apical mural thrombus** throwing emboli. ANCA-negative disease with the highest eosinophil counts is most at risk, needing urgent glucocorticoids with cyclophosphamide and anticoagulation while thrombus persists. **Systemic sclerosis** hearts scar differently: **cardiac Raynaud** vasospasm causes band necrosis that heals into fibrosis with ventricular tachyarrhythmias and diastolic failure.

steps.say: Positional chest pain with a rub is pericarditis in lupus until proven otherwise. PR depression with diffuse ST elevation is recorded on the ECG. Tamponade with hypotension and raised neck veins is drained urgently. NSAIDs with colchicine are given for uncomplicated episodes.
steps.tx: **Pericarditis** is the commonest cardiac lesion across rheumatic disease, found in up to **40 to 50 percent** of SLE autopsies and flaring in adult-onset Still disease with systemic JIA. Positional pleuritic pain with a friction rub and **PR depression** under **diffuse ST elevation** defines it, while hypotension with raised jugular pressure warns of tamponade. This figure is the display of the inflamed sac. **NSAIDs** with **colchicine** settle uncomplicated episodes, and tamponade physiology goes straight to pericardial drainage.

vis.alt: Medical illustration of acute pericarditis showing fibrinous exudate between the parietal and visceral pericardium generating an auscultatory friction rub, accompanied by an ECG showing diffuse concave ST elevation and PR depression.
vis.caption: Fibrinous pericarditis with friction rub and diffuse ST elevation with PR depression. Tamponade physiology needs urgent drainage. Credit: StewardMD.
